newsitem.title: USA: Rig count up four to 917 in week.
newsitem.headline: Rig count up four to 917 in week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 917 this week, up four from last week and 160 above the year-ago total of 757, oilfield services company Baker Hughes Inc. said Friday.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by two to 771, while rigs working offshore rose by one to 120. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose by one to 26.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Kansas, where there were seven fewer rigs, Pennsylvania, which was down by three and North Dakota, which was up by two.

A total of 368 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down six from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by 10 to 545, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at four.
There were 199 rigs drilling directionally, 64 drilling horizontally and 654 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 42 to 249, vs. 110 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, there were 171 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of May 16, up one from the period ending May 9, Offshore Data Services said.
